systems.system: Ghana Agricultural Information and Monitoring System

note: The only farming system named is run by a private firm for banks and investors, with no government, research-institute or early-warning part stated; the forest and flood tools are not farming.
Conference report on GIS use in petroleum and telecoms; nothing on satellite data for farming.
No farming satellite service stated for this country.

facts.fact: GEOGLAM's account by the project leads says the Ghana Space Science and Technology Institute and VITO are building the GEOMAIZE maize yield estimation from Sentinel-2 time series, with Ghana having a foundation for an operational pipeline.

systems.owner: Ghana Space Science and Technology Institute with VITO

facts.fact: SERVIR West Africa and the University of Florida report that GMet successfully tested initial operational capability of CRAFT for district-level maize yield hindcasts in Ghana, linking earth-observation crop type maps to production forecasts, with operationalising the service listed as a next step.

ESA states that VITO built Earth-observation crop classifiers from nearly 800 FSRP field points collected in August-September 2023, trained Ministry of Food and Agriculture officials in March 2024, and adapted a Ghana CLIMTAG dashboard, with Ghana planning to operationalise it in the GhAAP platform.

systems.owner: VITO for World Bank FSRP, used by MoFA and GMet

facts.fact: The Ghana News Agency quotes the Ministry of Food and Agriculture's public relations officer saying the ministry will deploy satellite surveillance capturing each enrolled Planting for Food and Jobs II farm twice daily to monitor planting and crop germination.

note: CORS network is for surveying and cadastral mapping, no farming use stated.
Only agritech startups using data and AI are named, with no satellite data or government service.
Space agency plan and general remarks on satellite use in cocoa lending and insurance; no government farming service stated.

facts.fact: The Ghana News Agency reports that the Germination Index Insurance has been piloted among maize, soybean and rice farmers in the Northern and Upper West regions, with rainfall data from stations of TAHMO and the Ghana Meteorological Agency merged with satellite data.

note: The 4,000 farmers sensitised are not stated as receiving cover or alerts.

systems.platform: TAMSAT satellite rainfall and TAHMO stations
systems.owner: Ghana Agricultural Insurance Pool with TEMBO Africa

note: An insurance product sold by insurers on satellite rainfall, with no government body named, is not a government farming service.
Host of a regional training; names no national service, study or pilot in this country.
Earth observation is only named as explored for SDG monitoring and natural capital accounting, not farming.

facts.fact: A CGIAR AICCRA infonote reports that satellite imagery from 2021 to 2025 shows significantly more vigorous crops in southern Ghana communities with climate-smart agriculture hubs than in control communities.
